newsitem.title: USA: Republicans wish Clinton well at inaugural lunch.
newsitem.headline: Republicans wish Clinton well at inaugural lunch.

text.p: Republican congressional leaders responded to President Clinton's call for bipartisanship Monday with warm wishes for a successful second term at an inaugural lunch they hosted for him.

"This is a joyous occasion. Here you are among friends. We wish you God speed in your administration," House Speaker Newt Gingrich told Clinton at the lunch in the Capitol after Clinton and Vice President Al Gore took their oaths of office at the building's west front.
Clinton, in his inaugural address, said Americans wanted the Republican-controlled Congress to work with his Democratic administration for the good of the nation.
"The American people returned to office a president of one party and a Congress of another," Clinton said in his speech.

"Surely they did not do this to advance the politics of petty bickering and extreme partisanship they plainly deplore," he said. "No, they call on us instead to be repairers of the breach and to move on with America's mission."

Republican Sen. John Warner of Virginia offered a toast for Clinton's success. He presented crystal bowls to Clinton and Gore as gifts from the Senate with an engraving of the White House and their names and the inaugural date, but noted Gore's bowl was a little smaller than the one for Clinton.
Warner said Clinton told him before the swearing-in began, "I'm more excited today than the first time."

Gingrich presented Clinton and Gore with U.S. flags that were flown over the Capitol Monday morning as gifts from the House. Clinton also received a framed photograph of the moment when he took his oath of office.
Four years ago when Clinton was sworn in for his first term, Democrats controlled Congress and were in charge of the inaugural ceremony.

Clinton thanked the Republicans and said, "I meant very much what I said about the bipartisan nature of our common task. And tomorrow we will start to work on it. For today I think we should all, as previous speakers have said, enjoy being Americans, enjoy the parade, enjoy the balls, but most of all enjoy the great gift of our citizenship."

New Republican National Committee Chairman Jim Nicholson also issued a conciliatory statement, saying, "On this Inauguration Day, Republicans join in congratulating President Clinton and in extending a hand of cooperation as we work toward our mutual goals of balancing the budget for our children's future, cutting taxes for working families and making government smaller and smarter."

Nicholson, elected last Friday, added, "At the same time, Republicans look forward to four years from today when we plan to celebrate the inauguration of a Republican president to work with a Republican Congress entering the next millennium."
